subsections.title: INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER NETWORKS AND PHYSICAL LAYER

topics.title: Networking Models (OSI & TCP/IP)
topics.content:
OSI Model (7 Layers):
- Layer 7: Application (User interfaces, protocols: HTTP, FTP, SMTP)[cite: 1].
- Layer 6: Presentation (Formatting, encryption, compression, formats: JPEG, SSL)[cite: 1].
- Layer 5: Session (Establishes, maintains, terminates connection dialogues)[cite: 1].
- Layer 4: Transport (End-to-end reliable delivery, protocols: TCP, UDP)[cite: 1].
- Layer 3: Network (Routing & IP addressing, protocol: IP)[cite: 1].
- Layer 2: Data Link (Framing & MAC addressing, error detection)[cite: 1].
- Layer 1: Physical (Cables, raw bits, signals)[cite: 1].

TCP/IP Model (4 Layers):
- Application (OSI 5,6,7), Transport (OSI 4), Internet (OSI 3), Network Access (OSI 1,2)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Networking Devices & Transmission Media
topics.content:
Networking Devices:
- Hub (Layer 1): Broadcasts data to all ports; creates network congestion[cite: 1].
- Bridge (Layer 2): Connects two network segments; filters using MAC addresses[cite: 1].
- Switch (Layer 2): Delivers data directly to target port using MAC table[cite: 1].
- Router (Layer 3): Routes data between different networks using IP addresses[cite: 1].

Guided Media:
- Twisted Pair Cable (Ethernet/Cat5/Cat6), Coaxial Cable (Cable TV), Fiber Optic (Light-based, ultra-fast, long distance)[cite: 1].

Unguided Media:
- Radio Waves (penetrates walls), Microwaves (line of sight), Infrared (short range, no wall penetration)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Functions & Error Control
topics.content:
Data Link Functions:
- Framing, Error Detection, Error Correction, Flow Control, and Access Control[cite: 1].

Error Detection:
- Parity Bit: Adds 1 bit to make total '1's even/odd (detects single-bit errors)[cite: 1].
- Checksum: Receiver recalculates segment sum to verify integrity[cite: 1].
- CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check): Uses polynomial division; detects burst errors[cite: 1].

Flow Control:
- Stop-and-Wait (send 1, wait for ACK) and Sliding Window (send multiple before ACK)[cite: 1].

topics.title: LAN Technologies, CSMA/CD, ARP & WLAN
topics.content:
LAN Protocols:
- Ethernet (IEEE 802.3): Uses CSMA/CD and MAC addressing[cite: 1].
- Token Ring (IEEE 802.5) & Token Bus (IEEE 802.4): Token-passing topologies[cite: 1].

CSMA/CD Mechanism:
- Listen before transmitting -> Transmit -> Listen for collisions -> Stop & send Jam signal -> Wait random backoff time -> Retry[cite: 1].

Address Resolution Protocol (ARP):
- Resolves IP Address to MAC Address[cite: 1]. RARP translates MAC to IP[cite: 1].

Wireless LANs (IEEE 802.11):
- Uses CSMA/CA (Collision Avoidance) instead of CSMA/CD[cite: 1].

PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol):
- Connects two direct devices (e.g., DSL/Dial-up) with authentication and error detection[cite: 1].

topics.title: IPv4 Addressing & Subnetting
topics.content:
IPv4 Addressing:
- 32-bit address represented in 4 octets (X.X.X.X)[cite: 1].
- Class A: 1-126 (Net bits: 8, Host bits: 24)[cite: 1].
- Class B: 128-191 (Net bits: 16, Host bits: 16)[cite: 1].
- Class C: 192-223 (Net bits: 24, Host bits: 8)[cite: 1].
- Class D: 224-239 (Multicast) | Class E: 240-255 (Experimental)[cite: 1].
- Reserved: 127.0.0.1 (Localhost), 0.0.0.0 (Default route), 255.255.255.255 (Broadcast)[cite: 1].

Subnetting:
- Divides large networks into sub-networks using subnet masks[cite: 1].

topics.title: Routing Algorithms & Protocols
topics.content:
Algorithms:
- Distance Vector (Hop count metric, RIP)[cite: 1].
- Link State (Full topology knowledge, Dijkstra's algorithm, OSPF)[cite: 1].
- Path Vector (BGP for Autonomous Systems / Internet Backbone)[cite: 1].

Protocols:
- IP (Connectionless, unreliable)[cite: 1].
- ICMP (Error reporting and diagnostics; ping, traceroute)[cite: 1].

topics.title: IPv6 Architecture
topics.content:
IPv6 Features:
- 128-bit address size (340 undecillion addresses) written in 8 hexadecimal groups[cite: 1].
- Built-in IPsec security, simplified header structure, auto-configuration, no NAT needed[cite: 1].
- Transition Mechanisms: Dual Stack, Tunneling (6to4), and Translation[cite: 1].

topics.title: TCP vs. UDP Protocols
topics.content:
TCP (Transmission Control Protocol):
- Connection-oriented, reliable, ordered delivery, flow/congestion control[cite: 1].
- Uses 3-Way Handshake (SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK) and 4-Way Termination (FIN -> ACK -> FIN -> ACK)[cite: 1].
- Used by HTTP (80), HTTPS (443), FTP (21), SSH (22), SMTP (25)[cite: 1].

UDP (User Datagram Protocol):
- Connectionless, unreliable, fast, no flow/congestion control[cite: 1].
- Used for Video Streaming, Gaming, VoIP, and DNS (53)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Ports, Sockets & Flow/Congestion Control
topics.content:
Ports & Sockets:
- Port Ranges: Well-known (0-1023), Registered (1024-49151), Dynamic/Private (49152-65535)[cite: 1].
- Socket = IP Address + Port Number[cite: 1].

Congestion Control Algorithms:
- Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit, and Fast Recovery[cite: 1].

Multiplexing & Demultiplexing:
- Mux (Sender): Combines application streams via ports[cite: 1].
- Demux (Receiver): Separates data to target applications using ports[cite: 1].

topics.title: Web, File & Email Protocols
topics.content:
Web Protocols:
- HTTP (Port 80): Stateless, plain text web transfer[cite: 1].
- HTTPS (Port 443): Encrypted web traffic using SSL/TLS[cite: 1].

File & Email Protocols:
- FTP (Port 21 Control, Port 20 Data): Plaintext file transfer[cite: 1].
- SFTP/SCP (Port 22): Encrypted file transfer using SSH[cite: 1].
- SMTP (Port 25): Protocol for SENDING email[cite: 1].
- POP3 (Port 110): RECEIVING email (downloads and deletes from server)[cite: 1].
- IMAP (Port 143): RECEIVING email (synchronizes and retains on server)[cite: 1].

topics.title: DNS, P2P & Network Tools
topics.content:
DNS (Domain Name System - Port 53):
- Translates domain names into IP addresses using UDP queries[cite: 1].
- Hierarchy: Root servers -> TLD servers -> Authoritative servers[cite: 1].

P2P Architecture:
- Decentralized model; every peer acts as client and server (e.g., BitTorrent)[cite: 1].

Monitoring Tools & Programming:
- Wireshark (Packet analyzer), MRTG/PRTG (Bandwidth graphers), SNMP (Device management)[cite: 1].
- Socket Programming: Creating network apps via client-server sockets[cite: 1].

topics.title: Security Principles & Attack Types
topics.content:
CIA Triad:
- Confidentiality (Encryption), Integrity (Hashing), Availability (Redundancy/DDoS protection)[cite: 1].
- Principles: Authentication, Non-repudiation[cite: 1].

Attacks:
- Passive: Eavesdropping, Traffic Analysis[cite: 1].
- Active: Masquerade, Replay Attack, Modification, DoS/DDoS, Man-in-the-Middle (MITM), Phishing, SQL Injection[cite: 1].

topics.title: Cryptography & Digital Signatures
topics.content:
Symmetric Cryptography:
- Single key for encryption/decryption (Fast; e.g., DES, AES)[cite: 1].

Asymmetric Cryptography:
- Public Key (encryption) + Private Key (decryption) (e.g., RSA, ECC)[cite: 1].

Digital Signatures & Email Security:
- Sender encrypts message hash using their Private Key; receiver decrypts using sender's Public Key for Authentication & Integrity[cite: 1].
- PGP (Pretty Good Privacy): Uses hybrid cryptography for email security[cite: 1].

topics.title: SSL/TLS, IPsec, VPN, WLAN Security & Firewalls
topics.content:
Network & Wireless Security:
- SSL/TLS: Secures TCP/HTTPS connections via certificate handshakes[cite: 1].
- IPsec: Network layer security (Transport & Tunnel modes; AH & ESP protocols)[cite: 1].
- VPN: Encrypted tunnel over public networks[cite: 1].
- WLAN Security: WEP (Insecure/Broken) -> WPA -> WPA2 (AES) -> WPA3[cite: 1].

Firewalls:
- Types: Packet Filter (Layers 3-4), Stateful Inspection, Application/Proxy Firewall (Layer 7), Next-Gen Firewall (NGFW)[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for physical transmission of data?
questions.explanation: The Physical Layer (Layer 1) handles the physical transmission of raw bits over communication media[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which of the following is a connectionless protocol in the TCP/IP model?
questions.explanation: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is a connectionless transport protocol that does not establish a prior connection before transmitting data[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which device operates at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: A Switch operates at Layer 2 and uses MAC addresses to deliver frames to specific destination ports[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the primary function of a router in a network?
options: To forward packets based on IP addresses
To connect multiple devices using MAC addresses
questions.explanation: Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network Layer) and determine optimal paths to forward packets between different networks using IP addresses[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which protocol is used for converting IP addresses to MAC addresses?
questions.explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) resolves logical IP addresses into physical MAC addresses[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which transmission media uses light signals to carry data?
questions.explanation: Fiber optic cables transmit data using light pulses instead of electrical signals, enabling high-speed long-distance communication[cite: 1].

questions.question: How many layers are there in the OSI reference model?
questions.explanation: The OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) reference model consists of 7 layers[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which OSI layer handles end-to-end communication and reliable delivery?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4) ensures end-to-end communication, error recovery, and flow control[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the primary function of a hub in a network?
options: To connect multiple devices and broadcast packets to all ports
questions.explanation: A hub is a Layer 1 device that unconditionally broadcasts all incoming data packets to every connected port[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which device uses MAC addresses to forward data directly to a destination port?
questions.explanation: Switches maintain an internal MAC address table to forward frames directly to the intended destination device[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which unguided transmission media has the shortest range and cannot penetrate walls?
questions.explanation: Infrared signals operate over very short distances and are physically blocked by solid obstacles like walls[cite: 1].

questions.question: In Ethernet (IEEE 802.3), what does CSMA/CD stand for?
options: Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection
Control Signal Multiple Access Collision Division
Carrier Signal Multiplexed Allocation Collision Division
Control Set Multiple Access with Collision Dispatch
questions.explanation: CSMA/CD stands for Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection, used in wired Ethernet networks[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which error detection method uses polynomial division and is effective at detecting burst errors?
questions.explanation: CRC uses polynomial division to compute a remainder checksum and is highly accurate at detecting burst errors[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which multiple access protocol is specifically used in Wireless LANs (Wi-Fi)?
questions.explanation: Wireless networks use CSMA/CA (Collision Avoidance) because wireless nodes cannot reliably detect collisions during transmission[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which protocol provides point-to-point direct communication between two devices at the Data Link Layer?
questions.explanation: PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) establishes a direct data link connection between two nodes, commonly used in dial-up/DSL links[cite: 1].

questions.question: What bit is added as a parity bit to '1010101' if using Even Parity?
questions.explanation: '1010101' contains 4 ones (which is even). Wait, count 1s in 1010101: 1, 1, 1, 1 -> 4 ones (even). To maintain even parity, 0 is added. If '1010' (two 1s) -> add 0[cite: 1]. For 3 ones, add 1. If 4 ones -> add 0.

questions.question: What is the size of an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: An IPv4 address consists of 32 bits divided into 4 octets[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which IPv4 address class range is 192.0.0.0 to 223.255.255.255?
questions.explanation: Class C IPv4 addresses span from 192.0.0.0 to 223.255.255.255[cite: 1].

questions.question: The IP address 127.0.0.1 is reserved as:
questions.explanation: 127.0.0.1 is the loopback address used by a host to send network traffic to itself (localhost)[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which distance vector routing protocol uses hop count as its metric with a limit of 15 hops?
questions.explanation: RIP (Routing Information Protocol) uses hop count as its primary metric and caps maximum path length at 15 hops[cite: 1].

questions.question: OSPF is classified as which type of routing protocol?
questions.explanation: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is a link-state routing protocol using Dijkstra's algorithm[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which protocol is used to exchange routing information between different Autonomous Systems across the Internet?
questions.explanation: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) is the standardized path-vector protocol used between different Autonomous Systems[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the size of an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long, formatted as 8 groups of 4 hexadecimal digits[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which protocol is used by the 'ping' command to test network reachability?
questions.explanation: The 'ping' utility relies on ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) Echo Request and Echo Reply messages[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the CIDR notation corresponding to the subnet mask 255.255.255.0?
questions.explanation: 255.255.255.0 consists of 24 contiguous set bits (8+8+8), represented as /24[cite: 1].

questions.question: Class D IP addresses are specifically allocated for:
questions.explanation: Class D IPv4 addresses (224.0.0.0 to 239.255.255.255) are dedicated to multicast communications[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which protocol guarantees reliable, ordered data delivery using a 3-way handshake?
questions.explanation: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a connection-oriented protocol providing reliable, ordered delivery[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which well-known port is utilized by HTTP?
questions.explanation: HTTP defaults to TCP port 80[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which well-known port is used by HTTPS?
questions.explanation: HTTPS (HTTP Secure) communicates over TCP port 443[cite: 1].

questions.question: SSH (Secure Shell) operates on which standard port?
questions.explanation: SSH uses TCP port 22 for secure remote terminal administration[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which transport protocol is preferred for real-time video streaming due to lower latency?
questions.explanation: UDP eliminates handshake delay and retransmissions, making it ideal for speed-sensitive real-time streaming[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the range of well-known port numbers?
questions.explanation: Well-known ports range from 0 to 1023 and are reserved for system services[cite: 1].

questions.question: In TCP, what does the SYN flag stand for?
questions.explanation: SYN stands for Synchronize, used to initiate connection requests during the TCP 3-way handshake[cite: 1].

questions.question: Flow control in TCP is maintained using which mechanism?
questions.explanation: TCP uses a dynamic Sliding Window protocol to regulate data transmission speed based on receiver buffer capacity[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which combination of parameters defines a socket?
questions.explanation: A socket is uniquely identified by the combination of an IP Address and a Port Number[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which protocol converts human-readable domain names into IP addresses?
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) translates domain names (e.g., google.com) into numeric IP addresses[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which application layer protocol is specifically used to SEND email messages?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is responsible for routing and sending emails[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which email retrieval protocol keeps messages synchronized on the mail server across multiple devices?
questions.explanation: IMAP keeps email messages stored on the server, synchronizing changes across all client devices[cite: 1].

questions.question: POP3 operates on which standard port number?
questions.explanation: POP3 uses TCP port 110 by default[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which packet analysis tool is widely used for capturing and inspecting network traffic?
questions.explanation: Wireshark is an open-source packet analyzer used to capture and inspect network traffic in detail[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which protocol supports secure file transfers encrypted over SSH?
questions.explanation: SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) runs over SSH (port 22) to provide encrypted file transfers[cite: 1].

questions.question: In a Peer-to-Peer (P2P) network model:
options: A central server controls all communication
Each node acts as both a client and a server
Only one active connection is permitted
questions.explanation: In P2P architectures, there is no central server; participating nodes act simultaneously as both consumers (clients) and providers (servers) of resources[cite: 1].

questions.question: What does the CIA triad stand for in computer security?
questions.explanation: The CIA triad represents the three foundational pillars of security: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a passive network attack?
questions.explanation: Eavesdropping is a passive attack because the attacker intercepts traffic without altering data or system operations[cite: 1].

questions.question: Symmetric key cryptography uses:
options: The same key for encryption and decryption
A public key for encryption and a private key for decryption
questions.explanation: Symmetric key algorithms use a single secret key shared between sender and receiver for both encryption and decryption[cite: 1].

questions.question: RSA is a popular example of which type of cryptography?
questions.explanation: RSA is an asymmetric public-key cryptosystem based on the mathematical difficulty of prime factorization[cite: 1].

questions.question: What security properties are provided by a digital signature?
questions.explanation: Digital signatures ensure message integrity, sender authentication, and non-repudiation[cite: 1].

questions.question: PGP (Pretty Good Privacy) is primarily designed to secure:
questions.explanation: PGP is an encryption program that provides cryptographic privacy and authentication for email communications[cite: 1].

questions.question: SSL/TLS operates to secure connection streams for which protocol layer?
questions.explanation: SSL/TLS provides channel security by encrypting reliable transport streams (TCP), such as HTTPS[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which Wi-Fi security standard is considered broken and insecure?
questions.explanation: WEP (Wired Equivalent Privacy) contains severe cryptographic vulnerabilities and is easily cracked[cite: 1].
